correctness.rationale: Exact counting formulas of two variables recover |G|, |G[3]| and |G[2^k]| for every k; successive 2-primary torsion ranks determine the invariant factors of Sylow-2. In odd factors every element has a unique square root, and the only distinct nontrivial atomic two-variable neighbors are square, inverse and square root. They coincide exactly for nonidentity order-three elements and are otherwise distinct, yielding uniform class-wise two-variable atomic-type multiplicities once the 2-component coordinate is fixed; induction over counting quantifiers gives sufficiency. Independently implemented all 27 substitutions of x,y,e into R on two nonisomorphic 50-element groups; simultaneous refined atomic-type histograms agreed for C2×C25 versus C2×C5×C5 (2 rounds) and disagreed for a 2-primary mismatch C4×C25 versus C2×C2×C25 (3 rounds). The finite color calculations do not establish the universal quantified claim, which rests on the symbolic multiplicity induction.
residual_risks: Only relational R with two variable names and named e; functional multiplication would invalidate the collapse.
The finite cross-check tested representative groups rather than a universal logical family.
